newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi.
E-mail:biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
INVESTIGATIVE AGENCY TRACES $7.8 MLN FERTILISER SCAM MONEY

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) announced that it had traced $7.86 million of National Fertilisers Ltd's (NFL) money in the Swiss bank accounts of two officials of Turkish company, Karsan. The amount is a part of the $37.62 million remitted by NFL to Karsan as payment for the import of 2,00,000 tonnes of urea. CBI sources said the new findings might help expedite investigations in the 1.33 billion rupee urea scam. They said the process for extradition of the two Karsan officials was on.
Indian Express
CBI MAY MOVE COURT FOR CHANGE OF JUDGES

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has decided to move a special leave petition (SLP) before the Supreme Court for a change in the composition of the Patna High Court bench hearing the fodder scam case. A High Court directive had divested CBI director Joginder Singh of supervisory powers in the case. The admission of the SLP in the apex court is expected to provide a reprieve for Joginder Singh and Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav.
The Pioneer
POLITICAL ATMOSPHERE TENSE ON EVE OF STATE POLL RESULTS

All major political parties are tense on the eve of the Uttar Pradesh assembly election results. Fortunes of more than 6,000 candidates in the politically-significant state will be decided when counting begins for 419 of the 425 Assembly constituencies on Wednesday. The outcome is expected to mould the future of United Front-Congress ties and the Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Economic Times
COMMUNIST PARTY FLASHES RED ON FOREIGN INVESTMENT POLICY

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has warned the government on its foreign direct investment (FDI) policy. The party, in a letter to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, has expressed concern about the coalition government's plans for allowing automatic clearance for FDI up to 51 percent in new sectors such as mining and textile manufacturing. The letter highlighted the danger of allowing automatic approval of 51 percent foreign equity for the strategic mining sector, which includes the mining of manganese, copper, chromite, bauxite and iron ore.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO DEFER LOAN CONVERSION

Poor stock market conditions and a decline in corporate performances have forced financial institutions to defer conversion of their loans into equity in more than 350 companies. Conversion of a loan component of over six billion rupees is due for conversion into equity in these companies. These companies include leading names like DCM Ltd, JK Corp, HEG, JCT Electronics Majestic Auto and Nippon Denro, among others.
BHARAT HEAVY ELECTRICALS SNAPS CONTRACT WITH ABB SWEDEN

Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) has decided to discontinue its technology transfer contract with ABB Sweden for high voltage direct current (HVDC) power transmission projects. The contract expired in May this year. BHEL is exploring several other options like floating joint ventures or using the licensing route to bid for HVDC projects.
Financial Express
NEW BIDDING FORMAT BEING EVOLVED FOR POWER PRODUCERS

The government is working on a new competitive bidding document for private power projects. Sources said the new document would utilise multiple parameters to determine the best bid. The tariff would not be the only determinant for selection of a bid. Independent power producers might now be provided with an indicative tariff rate which could serve as a benchmark for calculation of costs.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX GAINS 24 POINTS

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) witnessed wild fluctuations, even as the global depositary receipt (GDR) market for Indian stocks went to new lows for the third consecutive day. The BSE sensitive index closed 24.49 points higher at 3027.25 points, thus gaining on the GDR market, the Skindia GDR index touched yet another all-time low for the second successive day. At 55.97 points, the index fell 5.49 percent, indicating loss of 9.27 percent in the last one week.
FRESH PACKAGE TO LIFT SAGGING CAPITAL MARKETS PLANNED

The Finance Ministry is negotiating with the Securities and Exchange Board of India to evolve investor-friendly steps to boost the capital markets. The ministry has, however, ruled out financial sops for the market until the next budget. There will thus be no relaxation of taxation on dividend income or on capital gains in the current fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). But some concessions may be extended to capital market intermediaries to help facilitate borrowings from banks.
BAYER TO ACQUIRE 51 PCT STAKE IN ABS INDUSTRIES

German giant Bayer AG is making a 640 million rupee bid to acquire a 51 percent stake in Baroda-based polymer company ABS Industries. Bayer Industries, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bayer AG, will subscribe to a preferential equity allotment by ABS Industries and also follow it up with an open offer giving it a 51 percent holding in ABS. This is probably the first time in India that an acquisition is being made through the preferential allotment route.
The Observer
INTER CORPORATE LOAN CEILING MAY BE HIKED

The review committee formed for re-drafting the Companies Act, 1956 is planning to increase the combined ceiling on inter corporate loans and investment. The committee is considering increasing the ceiling from 60 percent of the subscribed capital and free reserves to 100 percent. The committee also intends to make the inter-corporate loans and investment interchangeable, thus abolishing the present provision to keep both loan and investment within the same limit of 30 percent of subscribed capital and free reserves of the lending/investing company.
FOREIGN INVESTORS MAY COLD SHOULDER BANKS ISSUES

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are unlikely to subscribe to new issues being floated by most of the nationalised banks. This is mainly because of the low premiums and the recent Reserve Bank of India letter to the custodians of FIIs asking not to allow them to invest in the secondary market of the State Bank of India scrip. This, in turn, might hamper the new issues being floated by most of the nationalised banks, banking sources said.
DECISION ON COAL TO HINDUJA PROJECT LIKELY SOON

A cabinet decision is likely to be taken soon to solve the problem of supply of coal to the Hinduja National Power Company. However, some more issues are likely to crop up which might delay the project even further, sources in the Power Ministry say. The power purchase agreement, being studied by the Union government after it was cleared by the Andhra Pradesh government, might throw up the question of working capital and the quantum of fuel which could be allowed to be stocked at the pit head station, sources added.
Business Standard
NORMS FOR REGULATING SHORT-SELLING TO BE TIGHTENED

The Finance Ministry has directed the bourse regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), to evolve more stringent norms for regulating short-selling. The existing SEBI norms dealing with price-rigging are sketchy when it comes to regulating short-selling. The ministry has now directed SEBI to amend these norms to specifically deal with short-selling. The move follows a steep fall in delivery-based trading on all the major bourses.
HUTCHINSON MAX GETS NOD FOR $150 MLN ADR

Hutchison Max Telecom has obtained the Finance Ministry's approval for mopping up $150 million through an American depositary receipts (ADR) issue. Hutchison Max, the joint venture between the Hong Kong based telecommunication major Hutchison Telecommunications and Max India, is the second Indian company to have received the ministry's permission for an ADR offering. Sources said the proceeds of the issue would be used to strengthen its cellular telephone network in Bombay.
FINANCE MINISTRY TO OPPOSE COGENTRIX POWER PROJECT

The Finance Ministry is learnt to have decided to oppose the controversial Mangalor Power Project. The project, being promoted by Cogentrix Inc of the U.S. and China Light and Power International, was recently cleared by a high powered board set up by the government. The Finance Ministry is said to be unhappy over the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) accepting the high heat rate demanded by the promoters. The ministry seems to believe that the CEA gave in to Cogentrix under pressure.
